turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so I don't have long. You gave my son a zero, and I'd like to hear from you why nobody called me first, Hale.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
Thank you. Now, who decided to enter the zero, and when was that decided relative to anyone speaking to Owen?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for acting against a student. So what else do you have, Hale, or is that all of it?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.
"Quite reliable." Okay. Your own school's procedure says software doesn't establish a concern by itself, so I'll ask again: what else do you have?
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." Procedure 4.2 says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Withdraw the zero, Hale.
I hope you understand my position.
"I hope you understand." Okay. My position is that Owen's essay got a zero from a score and nothing else, so withdraw it, Hale, or tell me what you have besides the number.
